superalloys.reasoning: Superalloys (Inconel, Hastelloy) are extremely work-hardening and abrasive. Ceramics run fast but shallow.

tips: Maintain chip load to prevent rubbing

tool_steel.reasoning: Tool steels are abrasive and wear-prone. HEM reduces radial forces and tool deflection.

tips: Ball nose with corner radius protection

stainless.reasoning: Stainless work-hardens rapidly. Must maintain constant chip thickness and stay engaged.

tips: Avoid air cuts returning to work-hardened surface

titanium.reasoning: Titanium's low thermal conductivity traps heat at cutting edge. HEM with proper engagement critical.

superalloy.reasoning: Extreme work hardening and heat. Must maintain engagement and remove heat immediately.

tips: Ceramic or CBN for extreme conditions

hardened.reasoning: Hard milling requires light radial engagement, higher speeds, ceramic or CBN tooling.

plastic.reasoning: Plastics melt easily. Use sharp tools, single flute or O-flute, control heat.
